title: Bell nonlocality from twisted statistics
authors: Ivana Đorđ ević, Jovan Potrebić, Aleksandra Gočanin, Dragoljub Gočanin
abstract: We investigate Bell correlations for a free real quantum scalar field on the noncommutative Moyal plane. Although the free field dynamics and the one-particle sector remain unchanged, the deformation enters through twisted multiparticle statistics and its Fock-space dressing representation. A classical external source coupled locally to the twist-dressed quantum field prepares coherent superpositions of momentum-pair configurations propagating toward two spacelike-separated laboratories. The momentum-dependent twist phases are generally nonfactorizable and generate entanglement between the corresponding wave-packet modes. We show that suitable local mode measurements lead to a violation of the CHSH Bell inequality. The resulting correlations provide an operational probe of the noncommutative structure encoded in the multiparticle sector of the quantum field.
summary: This work explores how noncommutative spacetime geometry, modeled by 'twisted statistics' in a free scalar field, can generate genuine Bell nonlocality. By analyzing the resulting two-particle state correlations, the authors show that measuring violations of the CHSH inequality serves as an operational signature for the underlying NC structure. This bridges quantum gravity phenomenology with fundamental tests of quantum foundations.
main_problem: Investigating whether Bell nonlocality can emerge from a quantum field theory structure modified by noncommutative (NC) spacetime geometry through 'twisted statistics.'
main_result: The violation of the CHSH Bell inequality ($S > 2$) is predicted, providing an operational probe for the underlying NC structure encoded in the multiparticle sector.
method: The analysis uses a relativistic Bell protocol setup involving two spacelike-separated laboratories and calculates the CHSH parameter based on state preparation governed by twisted statistics.
model_or_system: A free real quantum scalar field propagating on the noncommutative Moyal plane. The deformation is introduced via twisted multiparticle statistics, which modifies the exchange symmetry of creation/annihilation operators.
key_observables: Violation of the CHSH Bell inequality ($S_	heta$), and the non-local phase $\chi_	heta$ governing the entanglement.

main_assumptions: The state preparation is assumed to be local and causal, involving sequential pulses from a source in the common causal past.

paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first introducing the NC deformation via twisted statistics (modifying the coproduct/exchange symmetry), then applying this to a two-particle state preparation in a spacelike separated Bell test, and finally calculating the resulting CHSH violation.
why_interesting: It connects fundamental concepts of spacetime geometry (noncommutativity) directly to quantum information resources (Bell nonlocality), offering a novel theoretical tool for probing physics beyond standard QFT assumptions.
